destination.name: Coymanshuis
destination.note: The backlog row had a vague address ('Nieuwezijds/Singel area'); the real address was confirmed from nl.wikipedia (rijksmonument 2271). No installed model, manualCatalogue entry or landmarks.json/click-poi-info.json POI covered this pand.

facts: Facade designed 1625 by Jacob van Campen for Balthasar Coymans (plot bought December 1624); published 1631 in Architectura Moderna (Danckerts, De Bray).
Eight bays wide, with pilaster orders: Ionic on the bel-etage, Composite on the first floor.

Cross windows replaced by sashes c.1780, which removed the pediments above the first-floor windows; the original attic was replaced by a full storey in 1876 when it became a secondary school; the rear wall collapsed in 1931 and was rebuilt.
Amnesty International Netherlands head office since 2003; rijksmonument 2271 (register page not fetched, number taken from the Wikipedia article).

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012165021 LoD2.2, ground 0.957 m NAP, 21-vertex ring. The pand contains three canal fronts on one line: wall 9 (7.9 m, north neighbour, top 17.8 m), wall 13 (22.7 m, the Coymanshuis, eave 16.8 m) and wall 43 (8.2 m, bearing 284, south neighbour, top 17.4 m).
measuredBy.photoAxes: Eight window axes on the Coymanshuis, two arched doors on the middle pair, four rows (low cream ground storey, tall bel-etage, first floor, 1876 top floor); three axes with four rows on each neighbour. Heights read off ref-canal-front.jpg using the 3DBAG eave as scale.
uncertain: Right-hand (south) neighbour is cream/white painted; its row heights are scaled by eye because the wall turns away from the camera.
North neighbour's balustrade crown and cartouche are a simplified silhouette, not a carving.
Rear and side walls have no photograph (inferred plain brick); basement openings were not inventoried.
